title: Binary Search
summary: **Binary search** works when the search space is **sorted** or has a clear true/false boundary.
refresher: **Binary search** cuts the search space in half each step. It needs **sorted** data or a **monotonic condition**, where the answer switches direction only once. After checking mid, move past mid so the range gets smaller.

advanced-bs-sorted.title: Binary search needs order
advanced-bs-sorted.body: Ordinary **binary search** only works when smaller **values** are on one side and larger values are on the other.
advanced-bs-sorted.notice: The comparison at **mid** tells you which half can be ignored.
advanced-bs-sorted.mistake: On unsorted data, mid tells you almost nothing.

advanced-bs-mid.title: Mid is the test point
advanced-bs-mid.body: Mid is the **index** in the middle of the current low-to-high range.
advanced-bs-mid.notice: Mid changes as the range shrinks.
advanced-bs-mid.mistake: Do not keep checking the same mid forever.

advanced-bs-stuck.title: Move past mid
advanced-bs-stuck.body: When mid is not the answer, remove it from the remaining range.
advanced-bs-stuck.mistake: `low = mid` can get stuck when low and mid are the same.

blocks.body: **Binary search** only works when order gives meaning to the middle check. Because the data is ordered, one comparison can rule out half of the remaining positions.

sections.title: Move past mid
sections.summary: The range must shrink on every **loop**.

blocks.body: If `nums[mid]` is too small, everything at mid and to the left is too small. Move `low` to `mid + 1`. If `nums[mid]` is too large, move `high` to `mid - 1`. Mid was already checked, so the next range should not include it.

blocks.title: Avoid the stuck-mid bug
blocks.caption: Watch why `low = mid` can repeat the same range instead of shrinking it.

sections.title: Find first or last matching position
sections.summary: Some searches keep going after a match to find a boundary.

blocks.body: **Binary search** does not always stop at the first match. If the prompt asks for the first passing item or the last valid item, save the match and keep searching the side that might contain a better **boundary**.

blocks.title: Save a match and keep narrowing
blocks.caption: The match is a candidate, but the search keeps looking left for an earlier match.

sections.title: Binary search beyond arrays
sections.summary: You can **binary search** an answer range when true/false changes once.

blocks.body: **Binary search** can also work when you are searching for the smallest value that passes a test, or the largest value that still works. The key word is **monotonic**: once the answer becomes true, it stays true, or once it becomes false, it stays false.

blocks.title: Examples of monotonic questions
items: Smallest speed that finishes on time.
Smallest capacity that can ship all packages.

blocks.title: No boundary, no binary search
blocks.body: If true and false **values** are mixed randomly, the mid result cannot tell you which side to discard.

sections.title: Practice handoff
sections.summary: Write the range meaning before the **loop**.

blocks.body: Before coding **binary search**, write one sentence: `low` and `high` cover the possible answer range. That sentence helps you choose `<=`, `mid + 1`, and `mid - 1` correctly.

blocks.prompt: Why does `low <= high` matter in a closed-range search?
choices: It lets one remaining item still be checked
blocks.why: When low equals high, there is exactly one candidate left. It still deserves a check.
